patch.value: pm gc --scope runtime removes derived caches through a redirected runtime directory

Raised by the Codex review of the pm-gh1664 change on 2026-11-20. The runtime gc scope removes registry targets such as runtime/test-runs, runtime/history-drift-cache.json and, since pm-gh1664, runtime/history-stream-summary.json by joining them under the tracker root and removing them. If runtime/ is a symbolic link or Windows junction, the removal follows it and deletes files outside the tracker. The new stream summary's own reads and writes already refuse a redirected runtime directory (lstat must report a real directory), as does the context-usage ledger (src/sdk/context/usage-ledger.ts, docs/BOUNDED_CONTEXT_READS.md), but the gc registry path predates that rule and applies to every runtime target. Duplicate check: searched gc runtime, redirected runtime, symlink, junction and gc follow; no item owns it.

pm gc refuses to remove any runtime-scope target when runtime/ is not a real directory (lstat) and reports a warning naming the redirected directory; existing removals of real runtime targets are unchanged; a spec covers a symlinked runtime directory
Garbage collection never deletes outside the tracker
A symlinked runtime directory makes pm gc remove the targets inside its link target
